title: Clock rewind to the borrow phase
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word and let $c$ be a base configuration of the timed interpreter on input $x$. Let $u$ be a function assigning eight Boolean action bits, let $h$ be a Boolean halting flag, and let $b_s$ be a Boolean clock word. For every natural number $j\le |b_s|$, starting in the clock-rewind phase with clock word $b_s$ and clock head at position $j-1$, after exactly $j+1$ steps the interpreter is in the borrow phase with borrow flag true, the same clock word, and clock head at $0$.
replaced:
For every $j$ at most the clock word's length, from the clock-rewind phase
with the clock head at $j-1$, exactly $j+1$ steps of the timed interpreter
reach the borrow phase with the borrow flag set and the clock head at $0$; the
retained action bits and halting flag are unchanged.
